_comment: The nemotron Super-49B re-home, pinned as MEMBERSHIP rather than as a retirement. nano-gpt spells NVIDIA's Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1.5 with underscores, which the decomposition does not split on, so that row arrived with an empty variant and version and keyed the bare `nemotron#49b` line — which already held the genuinely different Super-49B **v1**. BOTH keys already existed before the pin, so the repair MOVES ONE INSTANCE AND RETIRES NO KEY: it is not a split, and it carries no migration table and no retired-key policy. This corpus is therefore not a retired-key corpus; each case names a LIVE key and the exact set of provider instances it must hold, spelled `<provider>|<model id>` with the id's upstream casing preserved. The two sets together are the conservation statement: four instances before, four after, none created, none dropped, none stranded. See TESTING.md.

provenance.ref: the bare 49B key must SURVIVE the re-home holding only Super-49B v1. Describing this lever as a split would be wrong: the key is not retired, and a test that only asserted the arrival on the v1.5 key could not tell a re-home from a retirement.

mutation.description: before the pin this key held TWO instances — the v1 row and nano-gpt's underscore-spelled v1.5 row, two distinct artifacts sharing one key. After the pin it holds the v1 row alone

provenance.ref: the v1.5 artifact is served from ONE key. This key already existed before the pin with the deepinfra and kilo rows; the pin adds the third spelling rather than minting anything.

mutation.description: before the pin this key held TWO instances (deepinfra + kilo, both dotted spellings). After the pin it holds THREE — nano-gpt's underscore spelling joins its siblings
